item.title: Update on West Kelowna water order expected Wednesday
item.description: On Monday, city staff conducted a reservoir inspection and cleaning. Once the cleaning is complete and the test results indicate there is no contamination, the reservoir will be refilled.

item.title: Oil prices rise and stocks fall as war with Iran advances despite Trump
item.description: With airstrikes still battering Iran and missiles still targeting sites across the Middle East, some of the optimism that sent stocks rallying the day before drained out of Wall Street on Tuesday. Oil prices got back to rising, and U.S. stocks are returning some of their gains.

item.title: B.C. mulls changes to weaken DRIPA, shares secret document with First Nations leaders
item.description: British Columbia Premier David Eby's government is considering amendments that would weaken a landmark reconciliation law that says the province will take "all measures" to align the rights of Indigenous Peoples with existing provincial legislation..

item.title: John Mulaney set to bring stand-up tour to Kelowna
item.description: Emmy Award-winning comedian John Mulaney is bringing his new stand-up tour, Mister Whatever, to Prospera Place this fall.

item.title: Wind, snow in forecast for Southern Interior Mountain Passes
item.description: A special weather statement warns southwesterly wind gusts up to 80 km/h will develop late Tuesday afternoon and peak in the evening.

item.title: Finland is the happiest country on Earth. Canada is 25th. How happy are you?
item.description: A new report says Canada has dropped down to 25th place in world happiness rankings, as researchers highlight heavy social media use contributing to a sharp decline in well-being among young people.

item.title: What to know about Cypriot calls for
item.description: Cyprus’ government is upset it was kept in the dark.

item.title: Four premiers ask for greater say in superior, appeal court judge appointments
item.description: The premiers of Ontario, Quebec, Alberta and Saskatchewan are jointly calling on the federal government to give them more of a say in judges who are appointed to their superior and appeal courts.

item.title: National Bank CEO urges Canada to move faster on priorities in
item.description: The chief executive of National Bank of Canada says he's not changing the bank's strategy because of the war in the Middle East, but he is urging a faster response from Canada to rising threats abroad.

item.title: Kamloops
item.description: ​​​​​​​Kamloops’ Matt Dunstone says his rink is primed and ready to take on top talent at the men’s world championship later this month.
